papers.title_en: Modification of Surface Properties in Ruthenium Thin Films through Nitrogen Ion Irradiation
papers.authors: Anmol Sharma, Arnab Tripathy, Rajeev Gupta, Raj Kumar, Harsh Vardhan, Ratnesh Kumar Pandey, Atul Thakur, Shalendra Kumar, Ranjeet Kumar Brajpuriya, Vishakha Kaushik, Sachin Pathak
papers.evidence: 离子注量驱动结构与表面演化
papers.tldr: 为调控Ru薄膜表面特性，本文用20 keV N+离子辐照100 Å与1000 Å两种厚度Ru膜，剂量约1e14–1e17 ions/cm2。随剂量增加，表面粗糙化并伴随接触角升高，出现亲水向疏水转变，1e17时接触角最高约95.54°。TRIM显示100 Å膜离子射程超出膜厚而触及衬底，1000 Å膜则基本限制在Ru层内；GIXRD表明结构改变、峰宽化及择优取向由Ru(101)转向(002)。
papers.abstract_en: Surface modification is an important strategy for tailoring the physical and chemical properties of materials for advanced technological applications. In thin films, changes in surface structure, roughness, and composition can strongly influence their functional behavior. In this work, we studied the effect of N+-ion irradiation at 20 keV energy on Ru thin films of two different thicknesses, 100 Å and 1000 Å, over a fluence range of ~1014 to 1017 ions/cm2. The main objective of this study is to investigate the evolution of the structural and wettability properties of Ru thin films of different thicknesses under increasing ion fluence. Overall, the results reveal that increasing ion fluence promotes surface roughening in both film thicknesses, which is correlated with an increase in contact angle. This indicates a clear transition from hydrophilic to hydrophobic behaviour, with the highest contact angle of ~95.54° observed at a fluence of 1017 ions/cm2. TRIM simulations reveal that for the 100 Å film, the projected ion range exceeds the film thickness, allowing interaction with the bottom substrate, whereas in the 1000 Å film, ion penetration remains largely confined within the Ru layer. GIXRD confirms fluence-dependent structural modification, including peak broadening with preferred orientation changes from Ru (101) to (002). Overall, this study demonstrates that N+-ion irradiation serves as an effective route for tuning both the surface morphology and wettability of Ru thin films, enabling controlled enhancement of hydrophobicity.
